title: Field install spotcheck and network quirks - Feb 2025
content:
Context and purpose:
Quick spotcheck write-up from the field install cadence (customer: 'PaperTrail / PTL') — capture small-but-real network/ops quirks we hit during the Feb 2-4 install window and immediate follow-ups for the on-call + install team. This is intentionally lightweight: raw notes, hypotheses, and next steps so SRE/infra can triage without waiting for a full postmortem.

Attendees / who was on-site + remote:
- Leona Rivera (on-site lead)
- Owen Brooks (network SME, remote)
- Marcus Patel (installer, on-site)
- Priya Nair (customer eng contact)
- Samir Gupta (private-deploy support, remote)
- Slack thread: #field-install-ptl (links referenced below)

Top-line summary (2 lines):
- Install finished functional; application processes started and model endpoints responded to test traffic, but we observed intermittent egress failures and elevated tail latency tied to customer network path MTU/fragmentation and an IPsec device rekey timing.
- Immediate mitigations deployed; long-term fixes require customer firewall rule tweak + SD-WAN firmware change and a small change to our sidecar backoff/timeouts.

Detailed timeline / observations:
- 2025-02-02 09:30 (local): Node provisioning and CNF images verified. No image checksum drift.
- 2025-02-02 11:00: Ran preflight (Confluence checklist) — VLAN, DHCP, DNS, KMS reachability green initially.
- 2025-02-02 14:20: First functional smoke tests (model load + token gen) passed locally on node but remote test calls from PTL app timed out intermittently (~1 in 7).
- 2025-02-02 15:05: Packet captures (tcpdump on node and customer edge) showed repeated ICMP Fragmentation Needed (DF bit + path MTU) when requests went through the customer SD-WAN -> internet breakout.
- 2025-02-03 09:40: During an IPsec SA rekey event on the customer's edge box, we saw a short (~25-45s) window of dropped UDP keepalives and SSH reconnects; this coincided with a background retry loop in our health-checker that amplified tail latency.
- 2025-02-03 13:10: Observed iptables rule on customer's NAT that SNATs ephemeral source ports into a small range (10240-10300) — caused ephemeral port exhaustion under our test burst.
- 2025-02-04 08:30: After applying a temporary MTU clamp on the node (1460), fragmentation ICMPs stopped and timeouts fell to near zero for the remainder of tests.

Hypotheses and root-candidate causes:
- MTU mismatch: Customer edge/SD-WAN path reduces MTU for encapsulated tunnels; nodes with default 1500 cause fragmentation and DF-triggered drops (ICMP indicates this).
- IPsec rekey timing: rekey window and short-lived NAT translation windows cause transient connection blackholes for short-lived TCP/UDP flows. Our short backoffs + immediate retries create bursts that exhaust the reduced ephemeral pool.
- Customer NAT/SNAT policy is intentionally narrow (security policy) but not sized for our default connection patterns (many short-lived outbound connections during model cold-starts).

Immediate mitigations we applied (temporary):
- Node-level MTU clamp to 1460 on all service interfaces (applied via installer script flag) — reduced fragmentation-induced timeouts.
- Small backoff tuning in the local health-checker: added jitter + exponential backoff (config flag dev/field-only: health.backoff.initial=120ms -> 250ms).
- Educated customer to temporarily widen SNAT ephemeral port range and to pin IPsec SA rekey window to non-peak install time.

Open blockers / tickets to escalate:
- JIRA PD-1184: Customer to confirm SD-WAN MTU and encapsulation overhead details and provide recommended clamp. (Owner: Priya Nair; due 2025-02-10)
- JIRA NET-902: Customer NAT ephemeral port range expansion required (security review pending). (Owner: Customer network team, escalated by Owen; due 2025-02-12)
- Action: File formal request to SD-WAN vendor to check for IPsec rekey bug that drops packets during SA rotation; if vendor confirms, plan firmware update. (Owner: Marcus; ticket created in vendor portal)

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Leona: Draft short runbook addition (how to MTU clamp + revert) and add to private-deploy runbooks. Due 2025-02-06. (status: in_progress)
- Owen: Follow up with customer for NAT/SNAT policy doc and confirm port ranges. Due 2025-02-05. (status: in_progress)
- Samir: Backport health-checker backoff patch to the last two GA releases and prepare hotfix PR. Due 2025-02-07. (status: todo)
- Marcus: Open vendor support case for SD-WAN rekey behavior; include packet captures. Due 2025-02-06. (status: todo)

Notes to self / informal learnings (short):
- For future installs, include a mandatory lightweight "encapsulation impact" preflight question: is there any middlebox (SD-WAN, IPsec, GRE) that will reduce MTU? If yes, recommend a default node-clamp of 1400-1460 until validated.
- Consider adding ephemeral port range check to our preflight script (fail preflight if ephemeral range < 5000 ports).
- Our health-checker model cold-start produces bursty connection patterns; we should add connection pooling or reuse for outbound dependencies where feasible.

Customer-facing summary (one paragraph we can send):
Thanks for the collaborative install window — core services are working now. We identified two network-level causes (MTU/fragmentation and narrow SNAT ranges) that produced intermittent timeouts during scale-up and rekey events. We applied a safe MTU clamp on the deployed nodes and adjusted local retry behavior; next steps are for your network team to widen the SNAT ephemeral range and for us to coordinate with your SD-WAN vendor on the IPsec rekey behavior.

References / links used during debugging:
- Packet captures (node): s3://redwood-ops/ptl/pcaps/2025-02-02-ptl-tcpdump.pcap (shared internal bucket)
- Preflight checklist: Confluence:private-deploy-preflight-checklist
- Slack thread: #field-install-ptl (2025-02-02 -> 2025-02-04)
- Jira: PD-1184, NET-902

Appendix: quick commands used in field (notes for runbook)
- MTU clamp (temporary): ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1460
- tcpdump tip: tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w capture.pcap host <customer-edge-ip> and filter icmp
- Quick check for ephemeral pool (customer): ss -tan sport = :10240-65535 | wc -l  (used to approximate port exhaustion)

If you want I can split this into a short customer email + internal runbook PR draft. Otherwise, will push the runbook patch by EOD 2025-02-06.

-- Leona R.
